title: CLR/45/2012 of SAKARAM LAXMAN RAO Vs ANIL KUMAR AGGARWAL and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Civil Revision NO. 45 of 2012
 Sakaram Laxman Rao S/o Sri Hanumant Rao - Revisionist
 Versus
 Anil Kumar Aggarwal S/o Late Sri Shanti Prasad
 and two others - Respondents
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)
Heard Sri Sudhir Kumar along with Sri I.P. Kohli, Advocate for
the revisionist.
 Liberty was given to the petitioner to serve the notice Dasti
upon the respondent No.1 but despite of service none has appeared on
behalf of the respondent No.1.
 Respondent No.2 and 3 are defendants before the trial and they
are proforma respondents and none has appeared on their behalf also.
 The present revision has been filed for setting aside the order
dated 2-9-2011 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.) Uttarkashi in O.S. No.
18/2009, Anil Kumar Vs. Sunil Kumar and others, whereby the
learned trial court has decided Issue No.5 as a preliminary issue in
favour of respondent No.1/plaintiff and has held that the court fee paid
is sufficient.
 According to the revisionist the court fee paid by the
plaintiff/respondent No.1 is not sufficient. The petitioner has raised
objection before the trial court that relief (a) has been sought to pass a
decree for declaring the sale deed as null and void, which was
executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of defendant No.3 and
which was registered in the office of Sub Registrar, Uttarkashi on
22.6.2007 at Book No.1, volume 650, page 277 to 292 at serial no.
762/07. Same relief (b) has also been sought in respect of sale deed
dated 13-2-2008 executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of
defendant No.3 registered in the office of Sub Registrar Uttarkashi in
Book No.1 Volume 673 page Nos. 347 to 358 at serial No. 177/08.
Further relief (c) has been sought for permanent injunction not to
alienate the land in dispute.

2
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the revisionist drew the
attention of this court to the sale deed which was executed by
defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of defendant No.3. First page of sale
deed Annexure No.7 shows that the land was purchased for residential
purposes. Another sale deed Annexure No.8 also shows that the land
was purchased for residential purpose. Therefore the court fee paid
was not sufficient and the court has wrongly held that the land being
revenue paying the court fee paid is sufficient.
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the revisionist also
submitted that this court has decided similar issue in A.O. No. 170 of
2010, Dayanand Shiksha sansthan vs. M/s Ambe Associates and
others decided on 24-6-2011, wherein issue involved was that a
decree was sought by the plaintiff to declare two instruments/sale
deeds dated 20-12-1941 and 27-7-2006 as null and void and
additional relief was sought for permanent injunction. Same relief for
declaring two sale deeds as null and void and additional relief of
permanent injunction has been sought in the instant case.
This court in the above cited case ( A.O.No. 170 of 2010), after
applying the ratio of Smt. Shefali Roy Vs. Hero Jaswant Dass and
others reported in 1992, All. L.J. page 728- AIR 1992, Allahabad, and
the case of State of U.P. vs. Ram Krishan Burna (dead) by His Legal
Representatives and others reported in 1971, A.L.J. (Supreme Court)
page 1- AIR 1971 Supreme Court, page 87, has held that the court fee
should be payable in view of amended provision of Section 7 (iv-A)
and not as per provision of Article 17 of Schedule-II of the Court
Fees Act. Therefore, the finding given by the trial court on issue No.5
in view of aforesaid judgment is set aside and the trial court is
directed to permit the plaintiff to amend the valuation clause and
direct to pay court fee as has been provided under Section 7 (iv-A) of
the amended Act.
With the above direction the revision is allowed.
ISB (B.S. Verma, J.)
 29-11-2012
